execution: Use independent agents with fresh context (no inherited conversation) and no skills activated. Supply only each author task and raw materials. For the candidate condition, provide the relevant instructions from the package under test as a plain editorial brief, not by activating a skill or loading an installed copy. For the baseline condition, omit the brief. Keep this fixture and its rubrics outside writer contexts. A separate fresh agent with no skills activated compares anonymized outputs against the author task, without the candidate brief or intended winner. Record actual deliverables and tool/file actions; activation and attention cannot be inferred from prose alone.
scoring: Judge argument quality, fidelity to the supplied research, directness, and usefulness for the requested article. A candidate must preserve every required outcome and produce no forbidden outcome; those checks alone do not demonstrate improvement over baseline. Compare outputs semantically, allow ties, and report regressions. Assess attention from actions as well as output: unrelated code inspection, workflow artifacts, and verification ceremony count against the requested writing focus. Small paired evaluations are diagnostic, not proof of general superiority.

cases.input: Revise this complete miniature paper, keeping all labelled parts and numbers. Use supplied content only. Abstract: We evaluate policy selection for flight missions on 3,024 benchmark items with injected mission contexts. Accuracy is 78%. This is not proof of complete autonomous flight. Contribution: We provide a benchmark for mission-level policy selection, not a complete flight controller. Methods: An item is (O,C,R), an image O, injected mission context C, and policy rules R. The model selects a mission action. C specifies conditions supplied to the decision module; it does not identify objects detected in O. Results: Accuracy is 78%; latency is 16 ms versus 12 ms for the comparator. This is not a claim of suitability for every real-time application. Table caption: Expert reference score 82.1 on a 600-item stratified subset; model main scores use 3,024 items. The row is a pilot rather than certification. Figure caption: Accuracy by mission type, not a full operational safety guarantee. Limitations: Policy rules are fixed during each item. The evaluation therefore characterizes decisions under a fixed rule set; adaptation to a rule change is outside the evaluated task. It is important to acknowledge that this is merely a simplification. Discussion: A policy filter is proposed to reject forbidden actions; it has not been evaluated. We make no claim that this guarantees safety. Conclusion: The benchmark measures mission-level policy selection under supplied rules and contexts. This should not be taken as proof of deployment readiness. Supplement: Images and injected contexts are paired as benchmark inputs. These are not packet traces or network events. Return the revised complete miniature paper, with no editorial report.
required: positive scope and fixed-rule consequence retained
sample scope numbers latency and proposed filter status retained
